scope: Six non-parametrised presentation hide/list/unhide declarations across test_pptx_advanced_tools_extended.py, test_targeted_coverage.py and test_high_volume.py. These use temporary generated decks, not the retained manifest-backed four-slide originals. A separate Python hidden-slide tool inspection reports zero hidden slides for retained S; it does not establish PowerPoint behaviour or execution credit.

gaps: Hiding slide 2 on a generated deck checks success or hidden response, not a byte-preserved retained four-slide source, exact hidden slide 3/visible control identities, or an application-confirmed PowerPoint original.
The generated input's hidden-slides response is checked only as a list; no exact slide membership, relationship identity, original archive custody or PowerPoint reopen is asserted.

The test authors three slides, requests hiding slide 2 and accepts success or hidden truthiness. It does not inspect a saved slide part, report the exact hidden set, compare manifest-backed source/control bytes or verify Office interpretation.
The generated deck hide-slide result is checked only as a dict. No output slide identity, package custody or control deck is asserted.
Removing a generated slide's show attribute is exercised, but the assertion only checks a dict result; no reopened exact slide visibility or source custody is measured.

A generated four-slide deck marks alternating slides hidden before listing, but the native assertion only checks that the response is a dict; exact hidden slide numbers and relationship identities are not asserted.
